50351597.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to FLAG-6His-Tev-ATAD2 (950 to 1148) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ATAD2 Surface Pl: SPR-based ligand binding assays were performed using a Biacore 4000 instrument (GE Healthcare) on CMS chips (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. Proteins were immobilized using standard amine coupling chemistry (10 min of activation with EDC/NHS, protein injection, and then quenching with 1 M ethanolamine, pH 8.5, for 7 min), with a running buffer of 10 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, and 200 μM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP), pH 7.4. 6His-FLAG-Tev-ATAD2(950–1148) was immobilized for 5 min at 75 μg/mL, immediately after 10-fold dilution into 10 mM sodium acetate, pH 5.5. The active-site double-mutant protein 6His-FLAG-Tev-ATAD2(950–1148/Y1021A/N1064A) was similarly immobilized, but for 7 min, resulting in 7–9 kRU immobilization for each protein. A third surface was activated and quenched without protein addition, and was used as a reference surface. Binding assays were then performed in 10 mM HEPES, 500 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% Tween 20, 1 mM DTT, and 1% DMSO, pH 7.4, at a 30 μL/min flow rate. Ligands were injected in a dose–response series (10 3-fold dilutions from 100 μM down), with solvent correction and positive/negative control cycles being used throughout the assays to control for differences in response to bulk refractive index changes and loss of binding activity from the surface, respectively. Dose–response data (from reference-subtracted curves) were fitted to a steady-state 1:1 binding model to determine K_D, and the results were compared to those from the active-site mutant protein to check for active-site binding.

(A) Equilibrium response as a function of the concentration. (B–E) Sensorgrams of the compounds.
